observationsNotFindings: The Why section pairs two sentences in parallel: 'Occupancy v3 remasured that already-named identifier' and 'signed-index leftover-join.v3 remasured that already-named identifier'. On the occupancy axis the remasurement (D-211) genuinely postdates the predecessor join's recording (D-188); on the signed-index axis D-178 precedes D-188, so frozen leftover-join.v3 was already stale on the DR-112 axis when it was recorded. The draft asserts no ordering — it states only that signed-index v3 remasured the identifier, which is true — and it names D-178 in the measured-inputs table so the ordering is recoverable. Claude Stage A examined the same point against the subject artifact and dispositioned it as not a finding. Recorded so the parallel construction is not later mistaken for an ordering claim.

The draft repeats v4's own paraphrase 'leftover-join.v3 cited signed-index leftover-join.v2 as the current DR-112 leftover-join'. Frozen v3's basedOn.signedIndexJoinV2.role does not use the literal word 'current'; it uses the definite article, cites no other DR-112 join, and states its measurements in live present tense. Stage A checked this paraphrase and accepted it as faithful. Not a finding against the draft.

File 08 carries 32 DR-G rows, of which three (DR-G05, DR-G17, DR-G30) carry dropped or deferred language, which does not arithmetically yield 28. The live required-now figure is the register's own condition-4 statement ('28 of 28 required gates name a recorded identifier'), which the draft tracks verbatim and does not alter. Recorded so the count is not mistaken for a discrepancy the draft introduced.

The Reversibility clause names D-086, D-188, D-211, and D-258 and omits D-178, although D-178 is a cited basis on the signed-index axis. This matches the immediate precedent: D-258's Reversibility clause likewise omitted D-170, the recording of its own cross-lineage ROW join. The draft preserves D-178's standing rather than unwriting it, so the omission carries no scope effect. Not a finding.
